findings.text: | S3-R1-02 | medium | tests/fixtures/agent-instruction-v1/evidence/family-profiles.json, scripts/agent_instruction.py:1495-1544 | Carried and filed sharply, because it is the shape of the fault this delivery exists to fix. `acquisition_sha256` digests rendered text, so it moves on a change that alters nothing that matters and would move identically on a change that alters everything: the same bytes-changed signal covers a cosmetic rendering difference and a genuine renderer or parser swap, and the operator cannot tell them apart from the digest. The only available response to either is a hand re-pin, which is what happened, and S3-R2-01 is what a re-pin under an indistinguishable signal costs. It was also the only field that could see the change at all: `_verify_profile_identity` checks `runtime_executable_sha256` at `scripts/agent_instruction.py:1506` and `version_sha256` at `scripts/agent_instruction.py:1527` before it reaches `acquisition_sha256` at `scripts/agent_instruction.py:1538`, and both survived the server swap, so `WAI-E-ADAPTER.EXECUTABLE_CHANGED` and `WAI-E-ADAPTER.VERSION_CHANGED` cannot fire on it. What a new pinned field would have to cover, stated so a carryover row can point at something real: the identity of the process answering on 127.0.0.1:11434, established before any measured or answered call, as a fact about the process rather than about text it renders; and the model's config blob digest, because `renderer`, `parser`, `requires` and the layer `diff_ids` all live there, it is content-addressed and stable, and pinning it would have rendered the August-to-September change as what it was -- config identical, difference in the renderer -- instead of as an opaque digest move. What it costs. The profile is a closed twenty-seven-field object at `scripts/agent_instruction.py:1946-1972`, so a new field is a version change to `wildcat-agent-instruction-family-profile/v1` and re-pins the same three bindings this re-pin moved: the profile, the manifest's `evidence.family_profiles` pointer and `TRUSTED_PROFILE_SHA256`. The config blob lives under `~/.ollama/models`, outside the repository root, and `read_confined` takes a root-relative path by construction, so the checker either gains a second read path with its own allowlist, which is a phylax boundary widening, or obtains the digest through the server and is back to trusting rendered text. And the field would do its job by refusing rather than being re-pinned, which means a genuine renderer change would block the delivery until a fresh `measure` and `parity` pair could be run -- a budget this run does not have. That trade is the finding: pinning the thing that matters makes an unrepeatable run refusable. Not step 3's: it changes a schema and needs a model run, so it belongs in the run's carryover as its own issue. | open |

Demonstrated rather than argued, in a throwaway copy: moving `documents[0].compact.tokens` by -5 and nothing else refuses `WAI-E-MEASURE.RECORD` at `$.evidence.measurement_record.documents[0]`, because `check` recomputes `one_document`, `totals`, `amortised` and every `measurement.result` event from `documents[*]`; moving the same count and every field derived from it, with the record's manifest binding rebound, exits 0 with no refusal and `totals.delta_tokens` reading `-170` in place of `-165`. `WAI-E-MEASURE.NON_NEGATIVE_DELTA` does not fire on either direction of that edit, so the one refusal the runbook names as able to end the delivery can be walked past by arithmetic alone. This is not a claim that the committed counts are wrong: round 1 recomputed every digest, byte count, correlation id and derived total in the record and all of them hold, and `-165` is honest arithmetic over the counts the run produced.
